title: Band-9 Samples: When you go shopping, do you prefer to pay for things in cash or by card? [Why?]
passage_text: This post contains ideas and band-9 sample answers (audio included) for the Cambridge IELTS 13 Academic Speaking Part 1 Question 1 Test 3 question: “When you go shopping, do you prefer to pay for things in cash or by card? [Why?]” Sample 1: In Cash Female Male I generally prefer to pay in cash when I go shopping. One of the primary reasons is that it helps me to manage my finances more effectively. When I have a tangible amount of money in my wallet, I can easily keep track of my spending and avoid impulsive purchases. Paying in cash gives me a sense of control over my expenditure. Sample 2: In Cash Female Male I have a proclivity for making cash payments while shopping. The primary rationale behind this preference is that it helps me avoid overspending. By carrying a finite amount of cash, I set a limit on my shopping expenditures, which encourages me to prioritize my purchases and strictly adhere to my financial constraints. Sample 3: In Cash Female Male I favor cash payments when engaging in shopping activities. A crucial consideration for me is the promptness and reliability of cash transactions. Unlike card payments, which can be hindered by technical glitches or connectivity issues, cash payments are a dependable option that ensures a seamless and uninterrupted shopping experience. Sample 4: In Cash Female Male In my shopping experiences, I find it more suitable to pay with cash because it is a widely accepted method, especially among local merchants who haven’t yet embraced card payment systems. This approach allows me to effortlessly engage with these retailers, promoting hassle-free transactions and a positive shopping experience. Sample 5: By Card Female Male In my opinion, I prefer to pay for my purchases using a card. The primary reason for this preference is the convenience it offers. With a card, I don’t have to worry about carrying a bulky wallet full of cash, and I can make transactions with just a simple tap or swipe. Additionally, using a card enables me to track my spending more effectively, allowing me to better manage my personal finances. Sample 6: By Card Female Male I am inclined to use card payments when I go shopping. This preference stems from the security that comes with using cards, as they often have fraud protection measures in place, ensuring the safety of my hard-earned money. Moreover, cards often offer rewards or cashback incentives, which can be quite beneficial in the long run, allowing me to maximize the value of my purchases. Sample 7: By Card Female Male I have a penchant for using cards when making purchases. This is primarily due to the fact that card payments tend to be more hygienic compared to handling cash. In today’s world, where health concerns are of paramount importance, paying with a card helps minimize the spread of germs and viruses, ensuring that I contribute to maintaining a cleaner and healthier environment for myself and others. Sample 8: By Card Female Male I opt for card payments while shopping, as I find them to be more efficient and time-saving. Cash transactions can sometimes be cumbersome, especially when dealing with change or waiting for the cashier to count bills. On the other hand, card payments are usually swift and hassle-free, allowing me to complete my shopping expeditions in a timely manner and focus on other important tasks. Sample 9: Both Female Male My payment preference while shopping oscillates between cash and card, based on the circumstances. For instance, when patronizing local markets or small businesses, cash is my go-to method, as it’s more widely accepted. On the other hand, when making substantial purchases or shopping online, I opt for cards due to the convenience of not carrying large sums of money and the added benefits like reward points or cashback offers. Sample 10: Both Female Male When it comes to shopping, I adopt a pragmatic approach and utilize both cash and card. I favor cash for day-to-day transactions, like buying groceries or dining out, as it helps me manage my budget and avoid overspending. Conversely, for major expenses such as electronics or travel bookings, I rely on my card to take advantage of the interest-free credit period and other perks associated with it.
